items.title: Donald Trump wants UFC fighters as assistants
items.standfirst: After a series of combative press briefings between the Trump administration and journalists, the US president surprised many by reportedly offering Dana White, the head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) and a longtime friend, the role of White House press secretary. Trump praised White as a “violent fighter and warrior”, but US media reports say he has already turned down the offer. Was it a punchy choice by the president or simply a punchline? Jack Pownall takes a closer look.

items.title: Middle East live: Israeli president officially tasks Eisenkot with forming government
items.standfirst: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Sunday officially tasked ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that or incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won a clear majority in Israel's October 28 elections. Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to form a coalition government. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments from the Middle East.

items.title: New Zealand's knife-edge parliamentary election delivers no clear winner
items.standfirst: No clear winner was produced in New Zealand’s legislative elections Saturday, setting up the two main blocs – Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition and opposition leader Chris Hipkins' left-wing alliance – for weeks of political wrangling to attempt to cobble together a majority. Hipkins said that while New Zealanders had spoken, "it may take us a little bit longer to figure out exactly what it is that you've said".

items.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least four
items.standfirst: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 30 miles from CairoAt least four people were killed and almost 90 others were injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, authorities have said.The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 30 miles south of Cairo, when a train travelling to the south-western Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transportation ministry. It said one of the trains derailed. Continue reading...

items.title: Paraguay: Senate impeached Peña rather than accept his offer to resign
items.standfirst: Paraguay's ousted president, Santiago Peña, has been charged over the collapse of Ueno Bank. Initially placed under house arrest, he has since been transferred to a military facility for his own safety. Nearly three million customers were locked out of their accounts after regulators seized control of the online bank. Repayments are now under way, but protests continue as customers demand access to their money. Peña denies any wrongdoing. Jack Pownall reports.
